newsitem.title: FRANCE: French beet conditions satisfactory - planters.
newsitem.headline: French beet conditions satisfactory - planters.

text.p: Growing conditions for sugar beets are satisfactory in France and prospects for the crop may further improve with the return of warmer temperatures, planters said on Thursday.
At this stage and despite nearly four months of drought, the crop potential was "still intact", they said.
The rain that fell over the last two weeks brought much-awaited relief to beets in most regions although moisture levels in Normandy and in the Auvergne area in centre France were still inadequate.
The return of warmer temperatures this week was also expected to speed up plant development.
"The situation looks good. Rain fell steadily over the last two weeks and warmer temperatures are back," an analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) said.
National sugar intervention board FIRS expects France to produce 4.20 million tonnes of beet sugar in the new season against 4.226 million previously, mostly the result of lower sowings.
